title: timeboxed telemetry primer and ephemeral debug shell
author: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Motivation: oncall responders frequently need a compact, high-signal telemetry snapshot at shift start or during early triage. Large, ad-hoc queries are slow, expensive, and often leak sensitive fields into chat channels. This PR introduces a timeboxed 'telemetry primer' utility that prefetches an annotated, minimal snapshot of critical signals and an ephemeral, read-only debug shell for safe interactive diagnostics. The primer is designed to be low-cost, privacy-aware, and attachable to incident threads via incident-bot.

What this PR does (single-string sectioned summary):
- Adds a lightweight CLI/service that collects a curated telemetry bundle (error rates, latency p50/p95 trends, recent sampled traces, active alerts, recent deploy markers, and a compact list of top 10 callers). The fetch window is configurable but defaults to the last 30 minutes (timeboxed).
- Introduces an ephemeral debug shell (read-only) that runs within a tightly sandboxed Lambda container: provides safe query primitives (schema-aware metrics, trace drilling by id, sampled logs) with rate limits, mandatory redaction rules, and an audit log per session.
- Integrates with incident-bot to publish a sanitized primer card to the incident channel and optionally attach a downloadable artifact. The incident-bot integration uses a feature flag and respects RBAC scopes.
- Adds CI tests, unit tests for sampling logic, property tests for redaction, and an end-to-end smoke test that runs against a local telemetry fixture.

Design choices and safety gates:
- Timeboxed default window (30m) with explicit override required for >2h fetchs; large-window fetches are blocked unless the user has the 'debug:extended' flag.
- Sampling-first approach: traces and logs are downsampled deterministically using a seed derived from incident id so multiple responders see consistent samples.
- Redaction pipeline: field-level allowlist/denylist implemented; PII-like fields are always stripped. The redaction rules are pluggable and live in docs/runbooks/telemetry-primer.md.
- Audit & retention: every primer run emits an audit record to the audit-log-exporter topic with a TTL. The actual artifacts are ephemeral and auto-delete after configurable TTL (default 24h).

Files and surface area changed (high level):
- cmd/telemetry_primer/cli.py: new CLI that produces the primer artifact.
- slo_toolkit/ephemeral_shell/shell.py: sandboxed interactive runner with read-only query primitives and guardrails.
- slo_toolkit/redaction/policies.py: declarative allowlist/denylist rules and unit tests.
- docs/runbooks/telemetry-primer.md: runbook and operational guidance for oncall.
- deploy/featureflags/primer-rollout.yaml: feature flag config for gradual rollout.
- dashboards/primer-summary.json: small Grafana template for primer summary panel.
- tests/test_primer_e2e.py: local fixture smoke test.

Checklist (completed):
- [x] Unit tests for sampling and redaction
- [x] E2E smoke test against fixture
- [x] Docs runbook with operator guidance and rollback steps
- [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan
- [x] RBAC checks and audit records

How to use (short):
- Run `telemetry-primer fetch --incident-id INC-12345 --window 30m` to get a sanitized artifact.
- Run `telemetry-shell start --artifact ./primer-INC-12345.tgz` to open a read-only shell that exposes `metrics`, `trace`, and `logs` primitives.
- If enabled, post to incident channel with `--post-to-inc-bot`.

Related work: links to the incident-bot integration RFC (internal) and ENG-5124 which requested built-in pre-triage snapshots.

Security notes: all network calls use instance-identity or KMS-backed credentials; the shell has no write APIs and runs with IAM role scoped to read-only telemetry. We added additional lint rules to prevent accidental removal of redaction steps.

Migration and rollout: feature flag start at 0.0.0 for beta, 10% rollout for engineering oncall, then wide. Default behavior is off for customers and on for Redwood internal oncall only.

review_comments: Ava Martinez: This looks useful. Two concerns: ensure the sampler is deterministic across responders and make the default window short to avoid cost. Can we add an override guard?

Sofia Nguyen: Reply: sampler is deterministic based on incident id seed; default window is 30m and there is an explicit guard that blocks >2h unless the user has debug:extended scope. Added tests for determinism.
Noah Kaplan: Please add an explicit audit record that includes the redaction policy version used. Also add a quick smoke dashboard so oncall can see primer health.
Sofia Nguyen: Reply: audit records now include redaction_policy_version and dashboard panel added (dashboards/primer-summary.json).
Priya Shah: Security review: verify that shell cannot access S3 write APIs and that credentials are ephemeral. Also request an approval from Security before wide rollout.
Sofia Nguyen: Reply: shell runs with read-only role, uses short-lived STS creds; added security checklist in docs. Marked rollout as internal only until Security approval.

Ava Martinez: Approving after seeing tests and docs.

(Approval: ava.martinez — 2026-03-04)
release_notes: Add telemetry primer for quick triage: timeboxed snapshot, ephemeral read-only debug shell, redaction pipeline, incident-bot integration. Feature-flagged; internal beta only.
